name: France: participant-facing document QC
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Trial title, short title, protocol number, EU trial number, sponsor and investigational treatment are correct and consistent.
States why the person is invited and whether the cohort is a patient or healthy-volunteer cohort.
Randomisation, blinding, placebo and treatment allocation are explained in language that matches the protocol.
Visit schedule, treatment period, follow-up, tests, procedures, devices and remote contacts match the latest protocol.
Routine care is distinguished from research-only procedures.
Benefits are not promised or overstated.
Foreseeable treatment, control, procedural and reproductive risks are covered without copying a technical safety table into the participant document.
Realistic alternatives to participation and planned care after the trial are described.
Contact routes work for routine questions, urgent safety matters, participant rights and privacy issues.
Every eligibility-sensitive restriction participants must follow is stated as in the protocol, including medicines, food, activity, contraception and donation restrictions.
Number and timing of blood draws, biopsies, imaging procedures, questionnaires and home activities match the protocol.

Sample types, analyses, storage, transfers, retention, optional future use and destruction are reconciled across the protocol, laboratory manual, consent forms and the biological-sample compliance template (FR-S1).
Data sources, recipients, transfers and retention are reconciled across the protocol, data-management material, MR-001 analysis and the participant notice.
Expense reimbursement and constraint indemnity match the EU compensation form (FR-P1) and the Additional France application document (FR-K-ADDITIONAL).
The insurance description identifies the correct France route and does not conflict with the certificate (FR-O1).
Pregnancy reporting and follow-up are described consistently in the protocol and participant documents.
items.applies_when: protocol has reproductive requirements or pregnancy follow-up

items.check: Main participation is separate from optional substudies, future research and any other choice that may be refused without losing trial access.
A clear yes and no choice is provided where an optional activity requires a recorded decision.
Genetic testing is not bundled into a general signature: separate information and express written prior consent for a genetic examination (FR-L1-GENETIC).
The recruitment and informed consent procedure (FR-K1) identifies who informs, who consents, when consent occurs and how understanding is assessed.
The participant has adequate time to decide, except where a legally valid emergency route applies.
Withdrawal effects are explained separately for trial procedures, new data collection, existing data and stored samples.
The participant receives a signed copy of the consent record.
Electronic or remote consent methods meet the same information, identity, signature, copy and record requirements and are described in the submitted procedure.

sections.title: Population and document coverage checks
sections.instruction: Build a list of every cohort and consent pathway in the protocol, then map an information version, consent form and recruitment route to each (see requirements.json population_sets).

items.check: Every cohort and consent pathway in the protocol maps to a population with an information version, consent form and recruitment route; populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage and each has its full document set.
Healthy volunteers: non-therapeutic purpose, exclusion period, payment, restrictions and national-register information.
Minors: age-adapted information, parent authorisation, personal adherence, refusal and re-consent at adulthood.
Limited-capacity adults: the exact French protective status is verified before selecting a legal representative or assisted-consent (curatorship) route.
Emergency enrolment: every Article 35 condition is addressed and later consent is sought without undue delay.
Capable participant who cannot write: the correct witnessed process and attestation are included.
Pregnancy follow-up: a pregnant participant is separated from a pregnant partner who is a new data subject.
Optional future data or sample use: separate choices, transfers, genetics and withdrawal are checked.
Controller, any EU representative and the data-protection officer or privacy contact are identified.
Processing purposes, data categories, sources, recipients, retention and participant rights are stated in clear French.
Direct collection under GDPR Article 13 is distinguished from collection through another person or record source under Article 14.
The selected legal bases are confirmed with the privacy team; trial consent is not equated with the GDPR legal basis by default.
The countries receiving data, the recipients or recipient categories, each transfer purpose and the adequacy status are listed as the France guidance expects.
Rights to access, rectify, restrict or object and the right to complain to CNIL are stated, subject to lawful research limitations.
What happens to previously collected data after withdrawal is explained without promising deletion that law or scientific-integrity duties do not permit.
The notice matches the MR-001 declaration or CNIL authorisation route stated in the Additional France application document (FR-R1, FR-K-ADDITIONAL).
Privacy text is checked in recruitment websites, screeners, apps, diaries and pregnancy follow-up forms, not only in the main consent document.

sections.title: Biosample and secondary-use checks
sections.applies_when: samples.collected or samples.archive_used or samples.future_use_outside_protocol or data.future_use_outside_protocol or genetics.examination_planned

items.check: Every sample, collection point, quantity or frequency and analysis is identified.
Storage location, access, coded status, retention, transfers and end-of-storage action are stated.
Protocol-defined analyses are separated from optional future research.
Any future purpose is specific enough to support an informed choice.
A changed sample purpose triggers a new-consent assessment before use.
The separate French genetic-testing information and consent form is prepared where a genetic examination is planned.
The main form, optional form and EU biological-sample compliance template use the same choices and terminology.
All participant-facing documents for France are in French.
The main information is clear, concise, fair and not so long that it impairs understanding.
The document identifies the CPP opinion and ANSM authorisation as required by French law.
The information explains the right to personal health information and access to overall research results.
Any constraint indemnity aligns with French restrictions and the EUR 6,000 cap over twelve consecutive months.
The data-transfer disclosure is exhaustive enough for the national Part II guidance.
The separate genetics route is used where applicable.
The recruitment procedure uses the harmonised version required on the intended submission date (version 2.0 from 1 September 2026).

sections.title: Signature, version and administrative checks
sections.source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/france/en/patient-facing-document-qc-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026); items C8.10 and C8.11 from content/playbook/naming.md and content/conventions/template-instructions.md

items.check: Each submitted file has a unique, consistent title, version and date.
The information-document version and date are on the consent page.
Signature and date fields are present for the participant and the person conducting the consent interview.
Parent, representative, curator, witness or separate data-subject fields are added only where the applicable route requires them.
Each role is labelled in French and it is clear whether a person signs for authorisation, assistance, attestation or consent.
Unsigned templates are uploaded at application; approved versions are signed during conduct.
Headers, footers, page numbers, blank pages, tracked changes, comments and hidden text are checked.
Filenames are intelligible in CTIS and PDFs contain searchable text.
Local contact placeholders are reconciled before site use through the approved document-control process.
Correct CTIS section and title per the naming guide and requirements.json (filename base without ( ) / , . ; | [ ]).

No drafting instruction remains in the final version (italic notes, [bracket] notes, ........... gaps, yellow [INSERT/IF/OTHERWISE/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); fields completed by hand at consent stay blank.
Plain French appropriate to the intended age, condition and health literacy.
Medical and regulatory terms are defined at first use.
Sentences and paragraphs are short and headings help a participant find an answer.
Legible type, contrast, spacing and page layout.
Diagrams and icons are explained in words where needed for accessibility.
No coercive tone, sponsor marketing language or statements that could waive legal rights.
An independent French reviewer has checked meaning, not only grammar.
Digital screens are tested on the devices participants will use and keep the CPP-reviewed content and flow.
items.applies_when: digital screens or electronic materials are used

items.check: No protocol fact, consent giver, optional choice, data transfer, sample purpose, payment or signature block is unresolved; each resolution is recorded and the affected checks rerun.
